newsitem.title: INDIA: India trade unions ask Chidambaram for tax relief.
newsitem.headline: India trade unions ask Chidambaram for tax relief.

text.p: Indian trade union leaders asked Finance Minister P.Chidambaram to abolish the limit on state employees' bonuses and income tax regime should be adjusted for inflation, a government statement said.

The statement, made available to Reuters on Sunday, said trade union representatives met Chidambaram for a pre-budget meeting on Saturday when they asked him to raise income tax limits to offset the impact of rising inflation levels.
Chidambaram is expected to present 1997/98 (April-March) budget around end February.
"Trade union leaders said that in view of the rising prices, the income tax limits should be suitably raised," the statement said.
They also asked him to abolish a ceiling on annual bonus payments to junior employees in government undertakings and state-run firms.
Last October about one million telecom and postal workers went on a nationwide strike demanding the abolition of a ceiling imposed by the government on annual bonus payments.
Trade union leaders also asked the finance minister to fix the minimum daily wage for the agricultural and unorganised labour at 60 rupees ($1.7).
They suggested that a national labour commission be set up for a good industrial policy, the statement said.
It quoted Chidambaram as stressing the need to increase revenues and reduce expenditure to keep the fiscal deficit at five percent of the gross domestic product (GDP).
Following are some of the issues raised by the trade union leaders in their meeting with the finance minister:
* Growth and investment should be made employment generating.
* PSU (Public Sector Undertakings) disinvestment should not erode the strength of these organisations.
* Greater functional autonomy for PSU boards. Memorandum of Understandings should be signed with management and workers.
* Sick fertiliser factories should be revived.
* Direct foreign investment upto 49 percent should be allowed in the core sector.
* Early implementation of Pay Commission's recommendations.
* Agriculture incomes should be taxed.
* Social security measures for rural workers.
* Concessions on tax on underground allowance for miners.
* Strengthen land reforms to help generate employment.
* Encourage agro-based and processing industries for employment opportunities in rural areas.
* Efforts should be made to recover loans from large bank defaulters.
* MAT (minimum alternate tax) should be retained.
* Plug loopholes that allow tax evasion.
* Greater incentives for the small scale sector.
